title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the notes 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', which follow La Longue Marche. Grothendieck studies the commutator map F_ρ : G → G, α ↦ [α,ρ], for a reductive group scheme G over a base S. The point is to solve equations [α,ρ]=ξ in which ρ is a distinguished element of SL(2,Z). On the next page ρ is the order-6 element (0 1; -1 1) and σ = σ_∞ = (0 -1; 1 0).

The mechanism, set up on the previous page, runs as follows.
- With [α,ρ] = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}, the equation [α,ρ]=ξ says ξρ = αρα^{-1}. So ξ lies in the image of F_ρ (fppf-locally) exactly when ξρ is fppf-locally conjugate to ρ.
- Conjugacy is tested through the adjoint (Chevalley–Steinberg) quotient map G → I_G (written G/int(G) → I_G).
- That map is an fppf epimorphism. It is neither a monomorphism nor injective on conjugacy classes in general. It does separate conjugacy classes of sections that are regular in Steinberg's sense in every fibre.
- For forms of SL(2), PGL(2) (written Gp(1)?) and GL(2), 'regular' means 'central in no fibre'.

This page computes I_G for groups of the form SL(E) or GL(E), with E locally free of rank 2. Here I_G is canonically the affine line E^1 or E^1×G_m, according as the reductive rank is 1 or 2.
- (7) For a form of SL(2): G → I_G ≅ A^1, x ↦ Tr x.
- (8) For a form of GL(2): G → I_G = G_m × A^1, x ↦ (det x, tr x).

Proposition. Let G be a form of SL(2) or GL(2) over S, and ρ a section that is central in no fibre. A section ξ lies (locally) in the image of F_ρ iff:
- (a) ξρ is central in no fibre, i.e. ξ ≠ λρ^{-1} fibrewise with λ central;
- (b) tr(ξρ) = tr ρ;
- (c) det ξ = 1. The margin adds: equivalently det(ξρ) = det ρ.
In modern terms: ξρ and ρ are both regular with the same image in G//G, hence fppf-locally conjugate.

Next page (corollary): when these conditions hold, the scheme of solutions α of [α,ρ]=ξ is a right torsor under the centralizer T_ρ. T_ρ is the unit group of the rank-2 algebra O_S[ρ], or for SL(2) its norm-one subgroup. Grothendieck claims T_ρ is smooth commutative of relative dimension 1 (SL(2)) or 2 (GL(2)). He then begins rephrasing forms of GL(2) as rank-4 Azumaya algebras M.
errors: Condition (c), det ξ = 1, is automatic for forms of SL(2). It is a genuine constraint only for forms of GL(2), where every commutator has determinant 1. The marginal 'équivalent à det(ξρ)=det ρ' only makes sense in the GL(2) case. So the parenthesis should read 'si G forme de Gl(2)'. The manuscript letter is overwritten (looks like Gl), and the machine transcription's 'Sl(2)' is likely a misreading or a slip.
'(suivant que le rang est 1 ou 2)' refers to the reductive rank of the group (SL2: 1, GL2: 2), not to the rank of E, which is 2 in both cases.

Related gap (next-page corollary): for forms of SL(2), T_ρ need not be smooth over a base with residue characteristic 2. Over F_2, the centralizer of σ (trace 0) or of a regular unipotent in SL2 is non-reduced, e.g. μ2×G_a. So 'lisse' holds for GL(2), but for SL(2) only away from 2 or for suitable ρ (for ρ of trace 1 it is fine). The torsor statement must then be read fppf-locally with a flat but non-smooth group.

'Il faut et il suffit' implicitly requires fppf-local conjugacy of fibrewise-regular sections over an arbitrary base. This is true for GL2/SL2 because the transporter is a torsor under the flat centralizer, but the page does not argue it.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct and fairly routine application of Steinberg's theory of regular elements and the adjoint quotient to GL2/SL2 over a base scheme. It serves the loop equations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. It is mildly interesting as a scheme-theoretic, Ngô-style 'regular centralizer torsor' viewpoint on the loop equations, but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Condition c): the image appears to read '(si G forme de Gl(2))', with the G overwritten, rather than 'Sl(2)'. This is consistent with the marginal note det(ξρ)=det ρ.
'(provisoirement)' after 'On trouve donc' is uncertain; it could be '(pour mémoire)'.
In (7) the arrow label is a crossed-out 'Tr'; the map is x ↦ Tr x into I_G ≅ E^1 (the affine line A^1).
In (8), E^{1*} denotes G_m (the affine line minus the origin), so I_G = G_m × A^1.
